name: World History Map
description: An interactive atlas of shifting political borders, states, and empires from 3400 BCE to 2024 CE.
overview: Explore 5,400 years of shifting empires, borders, and civilizations on a fluid 3D globe or flat historical atlas.

features.title: 3D Globe & 2D Atlas
features.copy: Morph smoothly between a spherical Earth in space with atmospheric glow and a flat Mercator map, with drag, tilt, and compass reset.

features.title: 5,400-Year Timeline
features.copy: Scrub the year slider, step by 1, 10, or 100 years, type any year directly, or press play to watch borders evolve automatically.

features.title: Thematic Color Lenses
features.copy: Recolor the world by distinct states, religion, political system, economy, or labor system—with custom color pickers and multi-select legend filters.

features.title: Switchable Base Layers
features.copy: Cycle between modern Positron cartography, orbital satellite imagery, or clean natural terrain with zero modern borders.

features.title: State & Empire Profiles
features.copy: Click any territory or search the active-states sidebar to view its lifespan, governance, religion, economy, capital, population estimate, area, and Wikipedia link.

features.title: Works Anywhere
features.copy: Runs directly in the browser on desktop or mobile and installs to your home screen as a fullscreen web app.

sections.title: Tours that talk you through the map
sections.lead: Choose from 99 guided tours and the map does the navigating—reframing borders for each moment in time, pinning the places that matter, and reading the story aloud.

items.title: Three Studio Voices
items.copy: Every tour is pre-recorded in Heart, Bella, and Michael—switchable at any time from the tour list or card, with Device voice as a browser fallback.

items.title: Stop-by-Stop Framing
items.copy: Each stop jumps to the right year, pins key locations, and fades the rest of the map into the background while keeping markers and notes intact.

items.title: Autoplay or Self-Paced
items.copy: Let autoplay read each stop as it opens, or turn it off to read at your own pace. Speech never moves the tour forward on its own.

sections.title: Every name links to the source
sections.lead: Place names and events across the app are live links that open in a new tab—keeping your exact year, zoom, and open stop right where you left them.

items.title: Wikipedia or Grokipedia
items.copy: Choose your preferred encyclopedia once in Menu & Layers and every link across the app—including tour and date cards—follows your choice.

items.title: Never Lose Your Spot
items.copy: Articles open in a separate tab so you can follow a thread as far as it goes and return straight to the same map view.

items.title: Curated Further Reading
items.copy: Every tour carries a short Further Reading list of museums, universities, archives, and primary-source collections beyond encyclopedias.

credit: Border data from Cliopatria (Seshat Global History Databank, v0.2.1) with OpenFreeMap basemaps.
